Several third-party tools already do this, and none of the results show an official single-source feature from Anthropic, OpenAI, or Google.

- **sync-agents-settings** reads MCP server configs and CLAUDE.md instructions from Claude Code and writes them to Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, and several other agents. It also offers diff, doctor, and reconcile commands. It syncs MCP server configurations and instruction files (CLAUDE.md) from Claude Code to Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Kiro CLI, Cursor, and others.
- **mcpport** lists, lints, syncs, and converts MCP configs across Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and Cursor. It covers those four tools. Its sync is a dry run by default and backs up the target file before each write, which is the safest pattern of the group.
- **mcp-sync** (Rust crate and PyPI/npm variants exist, with differing feature sets) keeps one canonical file and pushes it out. One variant establishes a single local source of truth at ~/.config/mcp-sync/config.json. The PyPI version manages global and project config files, with mcp-sync scan to discover existing configs.
- **mcp-config-manager** supports Claude, Gemini, and Codex with a sync mode. Its README lists the Codex config as ~/.codex.json, which doesn't match the TOML path Codex uses, so verify it before trusting it.

The main obstacles are format and path differences:
- Config locations differ. Claude Code uses ~/.claude.json and .mcp.json, Codex uses ~/.codex/config.toml (TOML), and Gemini CLI uses ~/.gemini/settings.json (JSON). The protocol is portable; the config is not.
- Field names differ for remote servers. Gemini uses httpUrl for streamable HTTP, while Codex uses url. Codex's TOML also has no string interpolation, while Claude's JSON supports ${VAR} expansion.
- Tool naming differs. Claude Code uses mcp__server__tool, while Gemini CLI uses mcp_server_tool.

Before adopting one of these tools, check its last-updated date, license, and whether it handles secrets. Credentials are the usual failure point when syncing. I didn't verify the maintenance status of each project.

**Supported agents:** Claude Code and Codex are listed. Gemini CLI is not mentioned. The page also lists Antigravity (a VS Code extension), OpenCode, and custom targets.

**Canonical config:** A single `mcp.yaml` file (default name, changeable with `--canon`), which can also be a URL. It has a `version`, optional `plugins`, and `servers`. Stdio servers take `command`, `args`, `env`, `cwd`, and `enabled`. HTTP servers set `kind: http` with a `url` and optional `headers`.

**Install:** `cargo install --path .` (run from a local copy of the source).

**First-run:** `mcp-sync sync` performs a one-time sync to all targets. The page also offers `mcp-sync init --output mcp.yaml`, an interactive wizard for creating the canonical file. It doesn't say whether `init` is required first.

**Preserves other settings:** Not stated. The `--clean` option removes servers that aren't in the canonical file, which implies only server entries are managed, but the page doesn't confirm that other settings are kept.

**Backups:** Yes. Before modifying any file, it creates a timestamped backup, such as `config.json` → `config.json.bak.20260105-230041`.

**Dry-run:** Yes. `--dry-run` prints the changes without writing files, and it can be combined with `--verbose`.

**License:** MIT.

content.content:
**Install:** Requires Node 22+. Run `npx mcpport <command>`, or install globally with `npm i -g mcpport`.

**First run:** The README suggests starting with `npx mcpport list` to see every server across agents, then `npx mcpport lint` to check for problems. To copy servers, run `npx mcpport sync claude cursor`, then add `--apply` to write the changes.

**Canonical list or copying?** There's no single master list. mcpport reads each agent's config, normalizes it into a shared format, and copies servers between agents with `sync` or `convert`. It also reports where the copies differ.

**Preserves other settings?** Yes, for the most part:
- JSON files keep keys unrelated to MCP.
- Codex TOML keeps comments and unrelated tables.
- `~/.claude.json` keeps non-MCP keys, and CRLF line endings stay CRLF.
- Gemini CLI JSON files that contain comments are read but never rewritten, so the comments aren't lost.

**Backups:** Before writing, the target file is copied to `<file>.<timestamp>.bak`. Writes go through a temp file and a rename.

**Dry run:** `sync` is a dry run unless you pass `--apply`. `list`, `lint`, and `convert` without `--apply` or `--out` are read-only.

**License:** MIT.

**Last commit date:** The page doesn't show it. It only says the repo has 14 commits.

**Stars:** 0 stars, 0 forks, and 0 watchers at the time of the snapshot.

**Install**
- **Claude Code plugin:** Run `claude plugin marketplace add Leoyang183/sync-agents-settings`, then `claude plugin install sync-agents-settings`.
- **npx (no install):** Run commands through `npx sync-agents-settings`.
- **Global npm:** Run `npm install -g sync-agents-settings`, then use the `sync-agents` command.

**First-run commands**
The page suggests starting with a read-only look: list your servers, preview the sync, then apply it. It also lists `sync-instructions` for CLAUDE.md files.
- `npx sync-agents-settings list`
- `npx sync-agents-settings sync --dry-run`
- `npx sync-agents-settings sync`

**Source of truth**
Claude Code is the single source of truth for MCP settings. The reader pulls from `~/.claude.json` and from enabled plugins' `.mcp.json` files.

**Preserves other settings**
Existing settings in target files are kept. The Gemini and OpenCode examples note that existing settings are preserved. Existing servers are never overwritten, so re-running is safe.

**Backups**
Each sync backs up affected config files to `~/.sync-agents-backup/<timestamp>/` before writing. Use `--no-backup` to skip this.

**Dry-run**
`--dry-run` previews changes without writing any files. The `/sync` slash command also shows a dry-run preview before applying.

content.content:
**Supported agents:** The page lists six targets: Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, Codex, and Kiro. It doesn't mention Claude Code or Gemini CLI. Codex covers the Codex CLI, the ChatGPT desktop app, and the Codex IDE extension, since they share one global config.

**Canonical file:** A JSON file at `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/mcp-sync/config.json` on macOS and Linux, or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\mcp-sync\config.json` on Windows. It has a `schemaVersion` of 1 and a `servers` map, where each server has a `command`, an ordered `args` array, and an `env` object.

**Install:**
- Homebrew: `brew install EnjoyableWork/tap/mcp-sync`
- Windows: `winget install EnjoyableWork.mcp-sync`
- Cargo: `cargo install enjoyable-mcp-sync`
- Or download an archive from GitHub Releases.

**First-run commands:**
1. `mcp-sync init` creates the canonical file and imports compatible server definitions.
2. `mcp-sync add <name> --command ...` adds a server.
3. `mcp-sync list` and `mcp-sync test <name>` review and check it.
4. `mcp-sync sync --dry-run`, then `mcp-sync sync`, applies it.
5. `mcp-sync restore <target>` rolls back a target.

**Preserves other settings:** Yes. Client-only fields, settings, comments, target-only servers, and unmanaged remote entries survive a sync. The page says there is no implicit pruning.

**Backups:** Each changed managed file keeps one adjacent `.bak` generation, replaced on the next change. Newly created files have no backup. Retention has no time-based expiration, so the page recommends copying files elsewhere if you need more history.

**Dry-run:** `mcp-sync sync --dry-run` validates and reports the redacted plan without writing anything.

**License:** MIT.

content.content:
**Canonical source:** `.ruler/ruler.toml`, using `[mcp_servers.<name>]` tables. Agent-specific servers go under `[agents.<agent>.mcp_servers.<name>]` and override global servers with the same name. The legacy `.ruler/mcp.json` still works but is deprecated. When both exist, TOML wins on name conflicts.

**Targets (all project-level):**
- **Claude Code:** `.mcp.json`
- **Codex CLI:** `.codex/config.toml`. For the local config, set `CODEX_HOME="$(pwd)/.codex"`.
- **Gemini CLI:** `.gemini/settings.json`

The page says: "Ruler never writes MCP configuration files outside your project root." It does not describe user-level MCP targets. The global `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ruler` fallback applies to rule configuration, not MCP output.

**Merge vs. overwrite:**
- Default is `merge`. Set `[mcp] merge_strategy` globally, or per agent with `[agents.<agent>.mcp]`.
- `--mcp-overwrite` replaces the native MCP config instead of merging.
- The page does not say exactly what a merge preserves in the native file.

**Backups:** Enabled by default. Ruler creates `.bak` files for pre-existing, non-Ruler-generated config files. Control this with `[backup] enabled`, `--backup`, or `--no-backup`. `ruler revert` restores from these backups.

**Dry-run:** `ruler apply --dry-run` previews changes without writing files.

**Other flags:** `--no-mcp` skips MCP application. `--no-gitignore` skips `.gitignore` updates.

**Install:**
- `npm install -g @intellectronica/ruler`, or `npx @intellectronica/ruler apply` for one-off runs
- Requires Node `^20.19.0 || ^22.12.0 || >=23`

**First run:**
1. `ruler init` creates `.ruler/`, `.ruler/AGENTS.md`, and `.ruler/ruler.toml` with sample MCP sections.
2. `ruler apply` distributes the rules and MCP settings.

**License:** MIT.

**Targets (all project-level):**

- **Codex CLI:** `.codex/config.toml`. For the local config, set `CODEX_HOME="$(pwd)/.codex"`.
- **Gemini CLI:** `.gemini/settings.json`

The page says: "Ruler never writes MCP configuration files outside your project root." It does not describe user-level MCP targets. The global `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ruler` fallback applies to rule configuration, not MCP output.

**Merge vs. overwrite:**
- Default is `merge`. Set `[mcp] merge_strategy` globally, or per agent with `[agents.<agent>.mcp]`.
- `--mcp-overwrite` replaces the native MCP config instead of merging.
- The page does not say exactly what a merge preserves in the native file.

**Backups:** Enabled by default. Ruler creates `.bak` files for pre-existing, non-Ruler-generated config files. Control this with `[backup] enabled`, `--backup`, or `--no-backup`. `ruler revert` restores from these backups.

**Dry-run:** `ruler apply --dry-run` previews changes without writing files.

**Other flags:** `--no-mcp` skips MCP application. `--no-gitignore` skips `.gitignore` updates.

**Install:**
- `npm install -g @intellectronica/ruler`, or `npx @intellectronica/ruler apply` for one-off runs
- Requires Node `^20.19.0 || ^22.12.0 || >=23`

**First run:**
1. `ruler init` creates `.ruler/`, `.ruler/AGENTS.md`, and `.ruler/ruler.toml` with sample MCP sections.
2. `ruler apply` distributes the rules and MCP settings.

**License:** MIT.

I recommend **sync-agents-settings**, which is free and MIT-licensed. It doesn't keep a separate master file. It treats your **Claude Code** MCP config as the one list and syncs it into **Codex CLI** (`~/.codex/config.toml`) and **Gemini CLI** (`~/.gemini/settings.json`). In practice you add a server once with `claude mcp add …` and then run one sync command. According to its README, it:

- runs locally with Node and needs no account
- keeps the other settings already in the target files
- backs up each file it changes to `~/.sync-agents-backup/<timestamp>/` before writing
- has a `--dry-run` preview, plus `diff`, `doctor` and `reconcile` commands

I'm assuming you mainly use servers at the user level (available in every project), not per-project `.mcp.json` files. I haven't tested this tool or any of the others below; these details come from their READMEs.

## Install and first run

You need Node.js and npm.

```bash
# Option A: try it without installing anything
npx sync-agents-settings list              # read-only: shows the servers it found in Claude Code
npx sync-agents-settings sync --dry-run    # preview what would change in Codex and Gemini
npx sync-agents-settings sync              # write the changes (backups are made first)

# Option B: install it globally
npm install -g sync-agents-settings
sync-agents list
sync-agents sync --dry-run
sync-agents sync
```

You can also install it as a Claude Code plugin, which adds a `/sync` slash command that shows a preview first:
```bash
claude plugin marketplace add Leoyang183/sync-agents-settings
claude plugin install sync-agents-settings
```

**Day-to-day use:** `claude mcp add <name> -- <command> …` adds the server, then `sync-agents sync` copies it to the other two.

**Before the first real sync:**
1. Make your own copies of `~/.claude.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml` and `~/.gemini/settings.json`.
2. Look over the `--dry-run` output. Pay attention to API keys and tokens in `env` and `headers`, because the sync copies them into the other files.
3. The README says it **never overwrites servers that already exist** in a target. If you later change a server's arguments in Claude Code, a plain `sync` may skip that server. Check `diff` or `reconcile` for those cases.
4. It's a small project (about 7 stars). Read the source or pin a version instead of running the latest from `npx` every time.

## Alternatives

| Tool | Best if… | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **[mcpport](https://github.com/Abdalkaderdev/mcpport)** (`npm i -g mcpport`) | You want the most careful writes | `sync` only previews unless you add `--apply`. It keeps Codex TOML comments and unrelated tables, and it won't rewrite Gemini settings files that contain comments. It copies between agents (e.g. `mcpport sync claude gemini --apply`) instead of keeping a master list. Very new, 0 stars. |
| **[mcp-sync (EnjoyableWork)](https://github.com/EnjoyableWork/mcp-sync)** (`brew install EnjoyableWork/tap/mcp-sync`) | You want a real standalone master file | Keeps the list in `~/.config/mcp-sync/config.json`, keeps other settings, and has dry-run and restore. **Its README doesn't list Claude Code or Gemini CLI as targets**, so today it only covers Codex for you. |
| **[mcp-sync (Rust crate)](https://docs.rs/crate/mcp-sync/latest/source/README.md)** | You want one master `mcp.yaml` | Supports Claude Code and Codex, but **not Gemini CLI**. |
| **[Ruler](https://github.com/intellectronica/ruler)** (`npm i -g @intellectronica/ruler`) | Your servers are per project | Writes one `.ruler/ruler.toml` out to all three agents, but **only inside the project folder**, never to your user-level configs. Well established. |
| **mcpm.sh** | — | A [PR adds Codex and Gemini CLI support](https://github.com/pathintegral-institute/mcpm.sh/pull/210/files), but I couldn't confirm it was merged. Check before relying on it. |
| [mcp-config-manager](https://github.com/holstein13/mcp-config-manager) | — | Its README gives the wrong Codex config path (`~/.codex.json`), so I'd skip it. |

None of these is a widely used, mature project yet. sync-agents-settings is the one that covers all three of your agents at the user level and is set up for this exact workflow.

- [sync-agents-settings](https://github.com/Leoyang183/sync-agents-settings)
- [mcpport](https://github.com/Abdalkaderdev/mcpport)
- [mcp-sync (EnjoyableWork)](https://github.com/EnjoyableWork/mcp-sync)
- [mcp-sync Rust crate README](https://docs.rs/crate/mcp-sync/latest/source/README.md)
- [Ruler](https://github.com/intellectronica/ruler)
- [mcp-config-manager](https://github.com/holstein13/mcp-config-manager)
- [mcpm.sh PR #210](https://github.com/pathintegral-institute/mcpm.sh/pull/210/files)
- [PyPI mcp-sync](https://pypi.org/project/mcp-sync/)
- [inventivehq: adding MCP servers to AI CLIs](https://inventivehq.com/blog/add-mcp-server-to-ai-coding-cli)
